doc.title: Joseph Daley interviewed by Monk Rowe, Utica, New York, March 18, 2018

title: Manhattan School of Music and the music education route
summary: A mentor and a plan B led him to Manhattan School of Music and a teaching job via the master's program.

story.theme_name: Teaching jazz: schools, students and advice to the young
story.community_name: Becoming a teacher: jazz in schools and conservatories

blocks.x: Did you have a moment or a period where you were going to decide to be a music educator or a music performer? Or was it the same?

Well what happens is that I had people that were — like I told you when I got into Music and Art I had a mentor. And he also went on to Manhattan School of Music also. So I kind of followed him into Manhattan School of Music also. So what I was told is that music is a tremendous pursuit and everything, but just have a plan B. So Manhattan had an excellent program. Manhattan School of Music had an excellent program where you can go four years as a performing artist, like do your juries and everything, and pursue a career in music as a performer. But if you decided the fifth year, when you went into your master’s program, the master’s program had two ways you can come into it — as a performer or you can come in as a music educator. So if you came in as a music educator and you — you did one year — first of all they got you a job, they got you a job immediately, and then you worked toward your license during that year. So you would teach during the day and then you would come to Manhattan School of Music afterwards and take your classes into the evening and everything. And then you were making a salary, you had health benefits, you started your pension and all that stuff, you know. So everything started that way. So I was receiving a check from the Board of Education. It wasn’t a lot of money, and I was finishing my studies at Manhattan School of Music, and I was working towards my teaching license. So when you graduated with your master’s degree you had a master’s in music education but you also got a New York City teacher’s license and you also had a position, a job, which if you were doing well as a student teacher then they took you on to become the full time director. So the principal of that school liked what I was doing and took me on, and actually my wife at the time too, she was doing the same thing in vocal music. She was in vocal music and I was in — so she got a job teaching vocal music in the same school that I did doing instrumental music.
